subject: Demo scheduling: Spring DST mismatch — LumenBank coordination
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Jenkins <mike.jenkins@lumenbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Mar 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Demo for billing optimization — initial timing options

Hi Mike,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to show how Redwood can reduce per-token inference costs for LumenBank's statement generation pipelines. We had penciled in a demo the week of Mar 9. A heads-up: that week includes the US daylight saving transition (Mar 9 in the US) while most of EU changes a week later. We want to avoid anyone on the call getting a shifted time.

Two clean options we recommend:
- Option A: Mon Mar 10, 14:00 CET / Mon Mar 10, 08:00 ET (works if you prefer EU-local time)
- Option B: Tue Mar 11, 09:00 PT / Tue Mar 11, 17:00 CET (earlier for West Coast engineering)

If you have APAC attendees, we can also propose Wed Mar 12 01:00 UTC as a single UTC-first slot. For safety we'll include explicit UTC times in the invite and attach an agenda + calendar stub.

Can you confirm which option works for your team and list any additional attendees (ops, security) so we can include a short prep doc?

Attached: agenda-20250305.ics (calendar stub)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

---
Vanessa Ortiz
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Jenkins <mike.jenkins@lumenbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenbank.com
Date: Mon, 03 Mar 2025 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo for billing optimization — initial timing options

Vanessa,

Thanks — appreciate the note about DST. A couple quick pieces of context from my side:
- We'll have three folks on the call: myself (payments), Priya Shah (security) and Rob Lin (infrastructure). Priya is in London, Rob is in NYC, and I'm in Manchester (UK).
- The week of Mar 9 is tricky because the US moves forward early on the 9th while UK/EU move later. That means calendar clients sometimes display different local times depending on timezone handling.

Option A (Mon Mar 10 14:00 CET / 08:00 ET) looks safe for the EU/US overlap for us. Can you confirm the invite will include the UTC time and mention "use UTC as the source of truth"? Also, can you provide a fallback plan if any attendee's calendar mis-parses the DST boundary (e.g., brief recorded walkthrough + Q&A window)?

If it helps, our preferred slot is Mon Mar 10 14:00 CET (we'd join at 13:55 GMT).

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Jenkins
Payments Platform Lead
LumenBank
mike.jenkins@lumenbank.com

Hi Mike — thanks for the preference.

We can lock Option A: Mon Mar 10 14:00 CET. A couple of operational notes so the invite doesn't get misinterpreted by different calendar clients during the DST handoff:
- We'll set the calendar invite using explicit UTC start/end times (Mon Mar 10 13:00 UTC — we list both CET/ET alongside).
- Add a one-line watchlist to the invite: "If your calendar client does automatic DST adjustments the week of Mar 9, use the UTC time as ground truth or join via the provided meeting link 5 minutes early."
- We'll record the demo and upload the short 20–25 minute walkthrough immediately after; that will be the fallback if anyone can't join because of a parsing issue.

I'm attaching our mutual action plan (MAP-LumenBank-2025-03.pdf) with the pre-demo checklist for Priya & Rob (security checklist + sample logs to have ready). Tessa will host the meeting and handle recording.

Proposed next steps: Vanessa — can you confirm and send the calendar invite with UTC + local labels? Mike — once invited, confirm attendees can see the UTC time on the event (quick screenshot works).

Thanks,
Karthik
